findings.title: Double interpolation when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates queries at line 52 via applyTemplateVariables(). It then passes these already-interpolated targets to runSplitQuery() at line 163. However, runSplitQuery() (in querySplitting.ts, line 299) also calls applyTemplateVariables() on its input targets. This means queries going through the shard splitting path are interpolated twice. While this may be idempotent for simple variable substitutions, it is wasteful and could produce incorrect results if a variable's resolved value contains text that matches another variable pattern (e.g., a label value containing `$` followed by text). Consider adding an option to runSplitQuery to skip interpolation, or restructuring so interpolation happens only once.

findings.title: Test mock mutates the input query object, masking potential double-interpolation issues
findings.body: The mock for applyTemplateVariables at line 56-58 mutates the query object in place (`query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)`) and returns the same reference. If the production code were to call applyTemplateVariables twice on the same object (which now happens due to the double interpolation path through runSplitQuery), this mutation-based mock would silently succeed on the second call (replacing an already-replaced string is a no-op), hiding the double-interpolation bug. A more robust mock would return a new object, making it easier to detect if interpolation is applied more than once.
